title: Rate limiter misconfiguration causing cascading 429s — action items and mitigations
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Summary:
On 2026-02-28 21:14 UTC we observed a sustained spike of 429 responses across multiple tenants in the US region. The spike lasted ~37 minutes and caused degraded UX for several high-volume customers (chat features and embeddings). Automatic remediation (circuit breakers) reduced tail but did not restore normal throughput until config sync from control plane completed.

Root cause hypothesis (confirmed):
A recent change to the rate limiter configuration format introduced a subtle field rename that caused the control plane to compute per-tenant capacity using an older fallback path. In normal operation the control plane writes definitive token-bucket parameters to the gateway and the gateways read those parameters via the config stream. Because some gateway replicas were slightly behind (config stream backpressure + a bug in reconnect logic), they used the fallback defaults which were globally conservative for some customers and permissive for others. For high-traffic tenants this produced token-bucket drift between replicas and an emergent behavior where the permissive replicas accepted bursts while conservative replicas rejected, triggering client retries and cascading 429s.

Why this escaped tests:
- Unit tests covered the renamed field in isolation but not the interaction with the config stream reconnect/backpressure logic.
- Integration test clusters did not exercise the multi-replica divergence pattern at realistic scale.

Impact and scope:
- Duration: ~37 minutes (partial mitigation via canary circuit-breaker after 4 minutes).
- Affected surface: Hosted API (US regions) — text generation and embeddings returned elevated 429 rates for ~12% of requests during the window.
- Customer impact: multiple customers reported degraded UX and higher error rates; three customers filed Sev2 support tickets.

Detection and mitigation chronology (abridged):
- 21:14 UTC: Pager alerts triggered for elevated 429 rate and SLO breach.
- 21:18 UTC: On-call identified config mismatch in gateway logs.
- 21:22 UTC: Temporary conservative global throttle applied to stop retries causing overload.
- 21:30 UTC: Control plane config stream reconnect fixed for lagging replicas; full parity restored by 21:51 UTC.

Postmortem conclusion:
The incident was caused by a combination of a config format change + fragile config stream reconnect/backpressure behavior that allowed token-bucket parameters to diverge across replicas under load. The cascading 429s were an emergent system-level failure, not a single-component crash.
action_items: AI-1: Revert the field rename patch in the control plane schema and release a compatibility shim to gateways within 48 hours (owner: gateway-config team, due: 2026-03-05).
AI-2: Implement strict config schema validation on both control plane writer and gateway reader; fail-open should be opt-in per tenant (owner: config-stream team, estimate: 3).
AI-3: Harden config stream reconnect/backpressure logic to ensure deterministic replay and backfill; add unit tests for reconnect edge cases (owner: infra, estimate: 5).
AI-4: Add an automated cross-check job that periodically computes per-tenant token-bucket hashes from control plane and gateways and alerts on divergence > 0.5% (owner: reliability, estimate: 5).

AI-5: Create a canary policy for rate-limiter format changes that includes staged rollout across gateway replicas and a rollback trigger based on divergence and 429 rate thresholds (owner: gateway-config + SRE, estimate: 3).
AI-6: Expand integration test harness to simulate multi-replica config skew under load and add a synthetic test that reproduces the token-bucket drift pattern (owner: platform-testing, estimate: 5).
AI-7: Update runbooks and on-call playbooks to include quick detection queries and an operator playbook to force parity without service restart (owner: SRE, estimate: 2).
AI-8: Notify impacted customers with a post-incident summary and commit to targeted credits for affected tenants; coordinate with CS and legal (owner: incident-comm, due: 2026-03-08).
